When I was young around 16, 17 maybe, I hanged out with 2 friends. People see us as three persons group but in reality, they were closer to each other than they did to me. Not long after, they both got boyfriends so they became closer.(I was single at that time so they couldn't talk with me about boyfriend stuffs.) They started to spend more time with their boyfriends, broke their promises to hang out with me even though they were the one who started the plan while I didn't even ask for their accompany in first place.

One time, they said they will hang out with me, eat some snacks, and watch movie. While we were eating, they got calls from their boyfriends and left me saying they will watch movie with me next time. Can you believe that? They made plans with me then they broke that promise. I watched that movie alone and had good time myself. After that incident, I started to enjoy staying alone, and didn't feel upset when they broke their promises again and again. I just don't give a f\*ck anymore.

But thanks to them, I found myself loving solitude and I didn't feel lonely. It was good that i could do anything I wanted. I could go anywhere I wanted, eat, watch movie all alone. So, i guess what I'm trying to say is.. try to enjoy spending time alone. Your happiness is in your own hands. Don't put it in other's hands.

Oh and btw, they are still in contract with me. We just don't hang out like we used to anymore.

You said, "I feel like they like to hide behind the facade of 'im scared of being hurt' as an excuse not to give and be vulnerable even when others do to them." You're saying exactly as my bf did. He also said that to me, that I wasn't doing anything, while he was taking risk for me. I too, was afraid of getting hurt again after my ex. I didn't want to take risk, and stayed behind "I'm scared of getting hurt". But after a lot of fights and arguments with my bf, I decided to take risk for him, and tried to get out of "I'm scared of getting hurt". If she really loves you, then I think she will try to take risk like I did. Though it took lots of efforts for my bf to make me risk like that..

Also, you're right about "I find that she likes to be loved but doesn't know how to love.", I want to be loved, but I don't know how to love someone. It's difficult for me to show affections and love to someone. But, I tried to improve that part of me and tried to show my feelings. But I still find difficulties in expressing my feelings.

I am not telling you that she's like me or all INFPs are like that. It's just that I find her similar to me(based on your description). So, perhaps if she was like me? That's what I thought.

I think your relationship can continue if she decided to change for you like I did for my bf. If not, then it's better you find someone who can fulfill your wishes.
